passage:
Archaeologists found remains of an old roadside inn. There were cooking areas, sleeping spaces, animal bones, and broken cups.
Students learned that travelers long ago also needed food, rest, news, and safety.
The inn made history feel ordinary in a good way. People moved for trade, work, family, and religion. They became tired. They ate. They listened to stories.
Modern travelers use hotels, stations, and rest stops, but the need is ancient.
The roadside inn showed that movement has always required places of pause. Travel history is not only about roads. It is also about where people stopped.
